Credentials for Google Cloud Storage

Source: R/auth.R
rcs_auth_gcs.Rd

Describes how the package reaches Google Cloud Storage. Pass the result (or a key file path) to the auth argument of store_connect() or store_create(); without auth, every Google Cloud Storage location uses rcs_auth_gcs(), the default lookup.

Usage

rcs_auth_gcs(key = NULL, token = NULL, fun = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'rcs_auth_gcs'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

key

Path to a JSON key file of type "service_account" or "authorized_user" (such as the file written by gcloud auth application-default login).

token

An OAuth access token with the scope cloud-platform. Not renewed.

fun

A function of no arguments returning an access token, or a list with access_token and expires_in (seconds). Called again when the token it gave is about to expire.

x

An rcs_auth_gcs object.

...

Ignored.

Value

An object of class rcs_auth_gcs: a list with source, type (the key file's type, or NA), file (or NA) and the environment cache. Aborts with class rcs_error_argument for invalid arguments and with rcs_error_backend for a missing or unusable key file. print() shows the source, type, file, identity and validity of the token, and returns x invisibly.

Details

Give at most one of key, token and fun. With none, the default lookup is a chain in which the first variable that is set decides:

  1. when the environment variable GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS is set, the file it names and only that file (a missing file aborts with class rcs_error_backend);

  2. else, when CLOUDSDK_CONFIG is set, application_default_credentials.json in that folder only (gcloud's folder is not tried);

  3. else the same file in gcloud's folder (%APPDATA%/gcloud on Windows, ~/.config/gcloud elsewhere), written once by gcloud auth application-default login;

  4. ambient credentials, when the file of step 2 or 3 does not exist: Arrow and the JSON API then use Google's own defaults (on Google Cloud, the metadata server).

Access tokens of a key file or a function are renewed five minutes before they expire, so a long session never signs in again. A token given with token cannot be renewed: it lasts as long as its issuer allows (usually one hour).

Asking for the same source again returns the same object, with its token. Printing the object never contacts the network and never shows a secret; the identity (the account's e-mail) is known after the first token.

Clients

One credential serves every client of a location: Arrow (data files), the JSON API (MD5 checksums), GDAL (rasters through /vsigs/) and DuckDB (store_duckdb()). Tokens, refresh tokens, client secrets and functions stay inside the object: they are never written to files, catalogs or logs, nor put in environment variables.

  • GDAL's options are process-wide. Reading a raster gives GDAL the credential of its location (a user login as the three GS_OAUTH2_* options, a service account as the GDAL option GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS, a token or a function as an Authorization header), for every GDAL read of the R process. The first switch to another credential warns (class rcs_warning_gdal_credential): a raster opened earlier reads its tiles lazily and may fail with the new credential.

  • DuckDB gets a temporary secret holding a token, in its connection only; call store_duckdb() again after about an hour of DuckDB work on a bucket to refresh it.

  • Ambient credentials work for Arrow and the JSON API only.

store_auth_check() tries every client on every location.

See also

store_connect(), store_create(), store_auth_check(); vignette("locations") for a walk-through.

Examples

# The default lookup; nothing is contacted until data is read.
rcs_auth_gcs()
#> <rcs_auth_gcs>
#> Source:   the application-default login of gcloud (default lookup)
#> Type:     authorized_user
#> File:     ~/AppData/Roaming/gcloud/application_default_credentials.json
#> Identity: known after the first token
#> Token:    none yet

# A token obtained elsewhere (here a placeholder)
auth <- rcs_auth_gcs(token = "<access token>")
auth
#> <rcs_auth_gcs>
#> Source:   an access token given to rcs_auth_gcs(token = )
#> Identity: known after the first token
#> Token:    given by the caller, not renewed
